name: Poured Light
description: An experimental neural-feed film with no narrative in the conventional sense — instead, the viewer inhabits a shifting series of anonymous bodies moving through GLMZ across a single day in 2207, experiencing the city as texture, temperature, smell, and social pressure rather than story. Director collective Lumen Void designed the experience so that the viewer's own emotional state at the time of viewing becomes the film's interpretive engine, meaning no two experiences are identical. Running time is officially listed as 'variable — between 55 and 190 minutes.'
cultural_impact: Established the 'city-body' genre of neural-feed art cinema and influenced a generation of filmmakers who began treating the viewer's nervous system as a co-author rather than a passive recipient.
story_hooks: One of the anonymous bodies in the film is carrying something — a package, a message, a memory — that becomes legible only after multiple viewings, and it's addressed to someone specific.
The persistent synesthetic episodes reported by some viewers aren't a side effect — they're a channel, and someone has been using it to communicate.
Lumen Void has disappeared as a collective; their final communiqué says they were 'inside the next project' and couldn't come back.
